body:
[A10] Assignment for #763 (author [A653]). Branch `763-map-persist` from dev e9cbb676.

1. An empty dynamic mapping list, and a non-empty non-default one, both survive a power cycle (Milan v1.2 5.3.9.1, 5.3.10.1).
2. The saved-state record must tell "empty" apart from "erased". Use a row count, or an empty marker that is not 0xFF.
3. Follow the saved-state contract and its records: docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md and the #70 erased-record rule. Bump any record version as the contract requires.
4. Add firmware unit tests and the saved-state tests for both cases, each with a planted mutant.
5. Run every gate the change touches, all rc 0. The firmware change needs the capture re-measure that the NVM capture check pins.
6. STOP on any change of the saved-state layout that breaks reading records written by the shipping image. If that is unavoidable, propose a migration and stop.

Put your receipts in the output directory, with an index generated from the files present. Post REVIEW READY or STOP on #763.

[A653] TAKEN
Branch: `763-map-persist` from dev `e9cbb676d7fdd6539aa408e5dfe38870a4ae1a5f`
Authoritative references: Milan v1.2 5.3.9.1, 5.3.10.1; docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md sections 4.2 and 6.1 (the erased-record rule); docs/design/SAVED_STATE_MATERIALIZATION.md sections 8.3, 8.4 and 18.4; #70; #637
Interpreted scope: make an empty and a non-empty non-default dynamic map list both survive a power cycle, with a record format that tells "empty" from "erased", firmware and saved-state tests for both with planted mutants, and every touched gate rc 0, under the assignment's STOP rule for layout changes.
Validation plan: the firmware AECP saved-state unit tests and their mutant campaign, scripts/check_nvm_record_space.py with its self-test, scripts/check_nvm_capture.py, and the docs gates.
Blockers: under investigation. The first reading suggests the shipping build has no channel-map record writer at all (#637), and that the record contract already separates an empty set from an erased record. I will confirm this or rule it out before editing anything.

[A653] STOP
Head: `e9cbb676d7fdd6539aa408e5dfe38870a4ae1a5f` (branch `763-map-persist`; no commits, tree unchanged)

**The suspected cause is not the board's.** On the shipping build (`milan_baremetal` with the processor in fabric; the `ctrl` firmware runs only under `--ctrl-mailbox`), nothing writes channel-map records. Records `0x60`-`0x7F` are therefore always erased, and the port reset set comes back. A non-empty non-default list reverts in the same way.
- The processor's D3 writer cannot form a map id. Its group bases are `0x00/0x02/0x0A/0x30/0x40/0x50/0x80` (`protocol-processor/hdl/aecp/KL_aecp_nvm_writer.sv:397-406`), and its header says it never writes or reads the maps (`:119-121`).
- In the parent, the maps have no record writer (`hdl/milan/KL_pp_shadow.sv:929-932`, `:949-951`). Stage 3 owns the map restore (`hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv:4452-4455`).
- The contract says the same: SAVED_STATE_MATERIALIZATION.md:17-20 (stage 3 not implemented) and SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md:1472-1476.

**The record format already separates "empty" from "erased"** (assignment item 2):
- An erased record is its whole span, header included, filled with `0xFF` (FASTCONNECT 6.1, the erased-record rule).
- An empty set is a framed record whose entries are all UNUSED (MATERIALIZATION 8.3, case V3g).
- The firmware store decides erasure from the header alone (`sw/firmware/ctrl_nvm/nvm_store.c:298`) and frames every latched payload (`:502-516`).

Changing to a row count or a non-`0xFF` marker would rewrite that accepted contract, the reference codec and record-space check 12 for no gain, so I did not attempt it.

**Executable check (scratch, not committed).** I ran a power-cycle test through the real store on the firmware AECP saved-state arm at `endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8`, once per direction. It empties port 0 by REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS and removes one row from the other direction's port 0.
- Clean sources: 8/8 `Nvm.*` pass, the new test included. Both lists survive, and the empty record is framed.
- Plant "`count == 0` keeps the defaults" in `aecp_nvm.c`: the test FAILS with the 8 defaults back.
- Plant "an all-`0xFF` payload reads as erased" in `nvm_store.c:298`: the test FAILS with the 8 defaults back, and **no in-tree test fails**. That is a firmware-path test gap, separate from the board defect.

**Why this needs a decision.** Meeting acceptance item 1 and the cold-cycle item on the board needs the parent map-record writer and restore. That is #637 (open, no lane), with acceptance in MATERIALIZATION 18.4, lane 4, which already requires empty sets on both directions and a cold cycle. It depends on lanes 1-3, DR3a, DR4 and #501. Building it under #763 would take over #637's lane.

Proposed decision:
- **A (recommended):** fold #763's acceptance into #637, and keep or close #763 as its board-acceptance item. Leave the record format unchanged.
- **B (optional, small):** narrow #763 to the firmware path. Commit the probe as an in-tree test in `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_aecp.cpp`, with the two plants as mutants in `aecp_mutants.py`. Gate: `python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_ctrl_firmware.py --require-rv32 --self-test`. No capture re-measure is needed, because `check_nvm_capture.py` pins `milan_baremetal.c` only. This does not fix the board.

The receipts (cited line extracts, the probe script, its logs and verdict, and a generated index) are in the lane's output directory.

[A10] Ruling on the STOP ([A653]): **both A and B.**

- **A.** The board's real gap is that nothing writes or restores the channel-map records, which #637 owns. Milan v1.2 5.3.9.1 and 5.3.10.1 make this mandatory, so #637 becomes a release item and gets its own lane next. #763's board acceptance (an empty list and a non-default list surviving a cold cycle) moves into #637's acceptance. The record format stays as it is: it already separates empty from erased.
- **B.** #763 narrows to the firmware path. Commit the probe as an in-tree test in `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_aecp.cpp`, with both plants as mutants in `aecp_mutants.py`, and run the firmware test gate. This closes the test gap the lane found: the all-0xFF plant failed no in-tree test.

#763 closes on B. #637 closes on the board.

[A653] REVIEW READY
Commit: `07c6c72fce79e705bcf28a70071497d0ce7040e4` (branch `763-map-persist`, two commits on dev `e9cbb676`; not pushed, as the assignment requires)
Changed (Round B, option B of the ruling):
- `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_aecp.cpp`: new `Nvm.EmptyAndNonDefaultMapsSurviveTheRealStorePowerCycle`, run once per direction. REMOVE_AUDIO_MAPPINGS (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.46) empties port 0 and removes one row from the other direction's port 0. The test commits through the real store and checks that the empty set is a framed record (magic `0x1722`) whose entries are all UNUSED. After a power cycle of the flash model, the emptied list must come back empty and the non-default list must come back as saved (Milan v1.2 5.3.9.1, 5.3.10.1).
- `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/aecp_mutants.py`: two named mutants. `nvm-empty-map-keeps-defaults` plants "`count == 0` keeps the defaults" in `aecp_nvm.c`. `nvm-unused-payload-reads-erased` plants "an all-`0xFF` payload reads as erased" at `nvm_store.c:298`. The campaign now copies the store beside its firmware copy so that the second mutant can be planted.
- `sw/firmware/ctrl/test/aecp_arms.py`: the saved-state arm compiles the store from the tree's sibling `ctrl_nvm/`. That is the same directory for the checkout and the planted copy for the campaign.
- `sw/firmware/ctrl/aecp/README.md`: documents both changes.
- No firmware source, record format, saved-state layout or RTL changed.

Validation (CPython 3.12.3, pinned RV32 SDK, pinned Verilator 5.050), all rc 0:
- `python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_ctrl_firmware.py --require-rv32 --self-test`: `test_ctrl_firmware: PASS`, 939 planted controls caught, none escaped, both new mutants `[ok]`.
- `python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_ctrl_firmware_shards.py`
- `python3 sw/firmware/gtest/tally_selftest.py`
- `python3 sw/firmware/gtest/fw_rv32_selftest.py --require-rv32`
- `python3 sw/firmware/ctrl_nvm/test/test_ctrl_nvm.py --require-rv32 --jobs 4`: 435 tests over 5 shapes.
- `python3 sw/firmware/gtest/fw_coverage.py --selftest` and `--check --jobs 4`: the ratchet is unchanged.
- `python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/ctrl_boundary.py --require-rv32 --selftest --without verilator` and `--only verilator`
- `python3 scripts/docs_check.py`, `check_feature_status.py`, `check_doc_style.py` (and `--selftest`), `gen_toc.py --selftest/--verify-anchors/--check`, and `check_em_dash.py --base e9cbb676`

Acceptance criteria (narrowed #763):
- Met: an empty list in both directions and a non-default list survive the store's power-cycle path, and the empty set is a framed record of UNUSED entries.
- Met: both plants are named mutants, and each fails the new test on its own diagnostic.
- Gap closed: with the new test excluded, the store plant passes all 73 other AECP app-arm tests and all six store suite binaries. No record-format change.
- Moved to #637 by the ruling: the on-board cold cycle.

Open risks/questions: `ci/image/tool-inventory.json` `--check` already exits 2 on dev `e9cbb676` (two unrelated script digests). This lane adds two more input digests to it (`aecp_arms.py`, `aecp_mutants.py`). That check runs in the CI image build, not in a pull-request workflow. I did not regenerate it, because that would fold unrelated drift into this lane. It is left to the inventory's owner.

Receipts, the handoff and the PR body are in the lane's output directory, with an index generated from the files present.

[A653] STOP
Head: `07c6c72fce79e705bcf28a70071497d0ce7040e4` (PR #766, branch `763-map-persist`; no new commit in Round 2, and the tree is clean)

Round 2 (PR #766 comment 6259259419) answers R658-1 (6258733493) and R657-1 (6259255660). Items 2 and 3 are done. Item 1 needs a decision.

**Item 1, the inventory refresh (R658-1-F1, R657-1-F1): STOP.** I ran the documented procedure (`docs/testing/CI_IMAGE.md:766-771`) with the pinned parser and did not hand-edit anything.
- `python3 scripts/ci_tool_inventory.py --write` changes exactly four `inputs` rows of `ci/image/tool-inventory.json`, and no `tools`, `residue` or schema field. Two rows are this lane's (`aecp_arms.py`, `aecp_mutants.py`). Two are inherited: `scripts/check_doc_style.py` (stale since PR #753, one `DOCUMENTS` entry) and `scripts/measure_test_evidence_readers.py` (stale since PR #754, one disposition entry). The generator rewrites all four in the same refresh. I reviewed all four script changes: none adds an installation request.
- Afterwards, `ci_tool_inventory.py --check` exits 0 (it exits 2 at the head), and the eight inventory and image self-tests at `CI_IMAGE.md:657-664` exit 0.
- **The conflict:** `tool-inventory.json` is a recipe input of the CI image (`ci/image/build.py:151`). The refresh moves the recipe digest from `712f7b38` (the value recorded in `ci/image/image.lock.json`) to `1e5e36f7`. So `python3 ci/image/build.py --work <dir> --check-lock` goes from 0 at the head to 2: "image lock does not describe the current recipe". Only an image build re-records the lock (`CI_IMAGE.md:665-667`). On `dev`, every inventory regeneration was followed by a lock re-record "from two byte-identical cold builds" (`e977cc44`/`cd9ef1be`, `ce3dd4bd`/`4df2f2f0`, `e19dd354`/`943d47db`, `f1c041bc`/`54fbcba6`).
- So the refresh alone cannot make every check that covers it exit 0. Committing it would swap the inventory refusal for a lock refusal, on a check that passes at the head today. I did not commit it.

Decision needed, one of:
- **(a) Recommended.** Commit the refresh in this lane as one generator-output commit. The image owner re-records `image.lock.json` on or before the merge candidate. The last re-record changed only `recipe_digest`.
- **(b)** Commit the refresh and re-record the lock in this lane. That means two cold builds of every image layer, far beyond this four-file delta.
- **(c)** Keep the refresh out of this PR, with a public decision and a tracking issue that give all four rows to the inventory's owner.

Separately, `ci/image/exec-audit-receipt.json` also holds the base digests of the two AECP scripts. It is a committed observation of one traced run inside the image (`CI_IMAGE.md:586-597`), so I left it unchanged.

**Item 2, the count (R658-1-F2): corrected.** The Round B evidence (comment 6258557430) said "939 planted controls caught". That overstated the planted controls. Classified against the AECP and SRP tables at the head, over the gate log (full log sha256 `375b9655…`), the 939 lines split as follows: firmware gate PASS; 876 source-mutant executions caught (520 control-source, 78 AECP, 278 SRP) and two pin-refusal controls passed; 61 normal arm outcomes passed (939 top-level `[ok]` lines). The PR body draft and the receipt summary now say this.

**Item 3, residue (R658-1-F3, R657-1-R1): applied** in the PR body draft. The status line now reads "two commits at published head `07c6c72f`". The roles name `[R657]` (internal, 6258585761) and `[R658]` (external, 6258590845). While item 1 is open, the draft says "Relates to #763" instead of "Closes #763".

Gates in Round 2:
- At the head: inventory `--check` exits 2, `--check-lock` exits 0, and the docs gates (`docs_check`, `check_feature_status`, `check_doc_style` and `--selftest`, `gen_toc` `--selftest`/`--verify-anchors`/`--check`, `check_em_dash --base e9cbb676`) all exit 0.
- With the refresh applied: `--write` exits 0, `--check` exits 0, the eight self-tests exit 0, and `--check-lock` exits 2.
- The firmware bank was not re-run. No byte in the tree changed since its rc 0 run at this exact head, and the refresh changes no firmware input.

No push, PR edit, Docker build, hardware or bench access was used. Receipts are in the lane's output directory under `receipts/round-2/`, with an index generated from the files present.
